mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about a compound is incorrect?

options.A: A compound is formed when two or more elements combine in a fixed proportion.
options.B: A compound can be separated into its constituent elements by physical methods.
options.C: The properties of a compound are different from those of the elements that constitute it.

mcqs.answer: A compound can be separated into its constituent elements by physical methods.
mcqs.explanation: Compounds can be broken down into their elements only by chemical reactions, not by physical methods. Options A, C and D are true statements about compounds, making B the incorrect choice.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best illustrates the difference between an element and a compound?

options.A: Gold (Au) and copper (Cu) are both elements; water (H2O) is a compound.
options.B: Gold (Au) can be broken into hydrogen and oxygen by heating.
options.C: Water (H2O) can be separated into hydrogen and oxygen by filtration.
options.D: Both gold and water are elements because they cannot be broken down.

mcqs.answer: Gold (Au) and copper (Cu) are both elements; water (H2O) is a compound.
mcqs.explanation: Option A correctly identifies gold and copper as elements (single type of atom) and water as a compound (two different elements chemically combined). Options B, C, and D contain false statements about how elements and compounds can be separated.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise that compounds have fixed composition
mcqs.question: Two samples of carbon dioxide (CO₂) are collected. Sample A contains 12 g of carbon. Sample B contains 24 g of carbon. Which statement correctly reflects the fixed composition of CO₂?

options.A: Sample B will contain 48 g of oxygen.
options.B: Sample B will contain 24 g of oxygen.
options.C: Sample B will contain 12 g of oxygen.
options.D: Sample B will contain 64 g of oxygen.

mcqs.answer: Sample B will contain 64 g of oxygen.
mcqs.explanation: CO₂ has a mass ratio of carbon to oxygen of 12 g : 32 g (or 3 : 8). Doubling the carbon mass from 12 g to 24 g also doubles the oxygen mass from 32 g to 64 g. Hence option D correctly shows the fixed composition. The other options give incorrect oxygen masses.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes a compound from a mixture?

options.A: In a compound, the components are present in a fixed ratio, whereas in a mixture the proportions can vary.
options.B: Compounds can be separated by simple filtration, while mixtures cannot.
options.C: Compounds always consist of metals, whereas mixtures contain non‑metals.
options.D: The boiling point of a compound is always lower than that of its constituent elements.

mcqs.answer: In a compound, the components are present in a fixed ratio, whereas in a mixture the proportions can vary.
mcqs.explanation: A defining feature of compounds is a fixed, definite composition; mixtures have variable composition. Options B, C, and D are scientifically inaccurate statements about compounds and mixtures.

mcqs.question: An element is best defined as:

options.A: A substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
options.B: A substance formed by the chemical combination of two or more elements.
options.C: A mixture of two or more pure substances.
options.D: A substance that can be separated by physical methods.

mcqs.answer: A substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
mcqs.explanation: Elements consist of only one type of atom and cannot be chemically decomposed into simpler substances. Options B and C describe compounds and mixtures, while D is false for elements.

mcqs.question: A compound is:

options.A: A pure substance formed when two or more elements combine in a fixed proportion and have new properties.
options.B: A mixture of elements that can be separated by filtration.
options.C: An element that exists in more than one form.
options.D: A substance that cannot be broken down by any method.

mcqs.answer: A pure substance formed when two or more elements combine in a fixed proportion and have new properties.
mcqs.explanation: Compounds are formed by chemical combination of elements in definite ratios, resulting in properties different from the constituent elements. Options B, C, and D describe mixtures, allotropes, or an incorrect absolute statement.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an element from a compound?

options.A: Elements consist of only one type of atom; compounds consist of two or more different atoms chemically bonded.
options.B: Elements can be separated by chemical reactions; compounds cannot.
options.C: Elements have variable composition; compounds have fixed composition.
options.D: Elements are always gases; compounds are always solids.

mcqs.answer: Elements consist of only one type of atom; compounds consist of two or more different atoms chemically bonded.
mcqs.explanation: Option A accurately reflects that elements are made of a single kind of atom, while compounds contain atoms of different elements chemically combined. The other options contain false statements about separability, composition variability, and physical state.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise that compounds have fixed composition
mcqs.question: If 18 g of water (H₂O) is completely evaporated, how many grams of hydrogen are present in the vapor?
mcqs.explanation: One mole of water (18 g) contains 2 g of hydrogen (since H₂ = 2 g). Therefore, 18 g of water vapor contains 2 g of hydrogen. Options B, C, and D overestimate the hydrogen content.
